entry.name: UMI-Dex-Pro-L6
entry.title: UMI-Dex-Pro-L6 Manipulation Dataset
entry.summary: A person carries the UMI-Dex-Pro-L6 right hand (L6-type, 6 DoF, no robot arm) with five 12x6 fingertip taxel arrays and per-finger grip force in mN, recorded with a wrist D405 camera and a VIVE Ultimate Tracker over 251 single-hand pick-and-place and cup-stacking segments.
entry.hand: UMI-Dex-Pro-L6 (Linker L6-type right hand, 6 DoF, fingertip tactile), carried by a person; no robot arm or body

sensor.note: /hand/touch_state (umi_dex_msgs/HandTouchState) at 60 Hz: touch_matrix uint8[360] = 5 fingers x 72 (12 rows x 6 columns, row-major, raw 0-255), finger_force_mn uint16[5] = grip force per finger in mN (0-65.535 N; thumb, index, middle, ring, little), plus hwk_valid_mask and force_valid_mask bits and a firmware seq that matches /hand/joint_states. The per-finger force is in physical units; the taxels are raw.
sensor.range: grip force 0-65.535 N per finger (uint16 mN); taxels 0-255 raw

scale.text: 251 segments, ~0.83 h, 5 right-hand tabletop tasks (stack 6 cups 50, nail 50, water bottle 51, apple model 50, green cube 50); segments 8.3-21.3 s; 51.1 GiB

entry.access: ModelScope Linkerbot/UMI-Dex-Pro-L6_Manipulation-Dataset, open download (git LFS or SDK): one uncompressed TAR per task (8.5-15.7 GiB) with one ROS2 MCAP bag + metadata.yaml per segment; HTTP range reads into the TARs work.
entry.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; commercial use needs written authorization
caveats: No robot arm or body ('UMI-Dex 无本体数据采集系统' [UMI-Dex robot-body-free data collection system]): a person carries the hand, and the wrist pose comes from a VIVE Ultimate Tracker, not from robot joints.

How the fingers are moved is not stated on the card; finger channels are 6 raw encoder readings (0-255, 'not radians or percent'). The UMI-Dex GitHub hardware folder describes an 'L6 6-DOF serial encoder glove' with finger and arm straps.
Touch is sparse: in 6 segments checked, only thumb and index pads registered; a nail-pinch segment showed no taxel above 0 and an apple segment peaked at 3 counts (sampled every ~0.5 s).
Taxel values are low (peaks of 14-22 of 255 on single taxels in the checked segments); per-finger force reached 0.98-1.2 N.

touch_matrix finger order is 'STM32_FINGER_ORDER' in the message definition; the card states thumb-to-little only for finger_force_mn. In the checked segments the matrix finger with contact matched the force channel with contact.
Right hand only; one operator count not stated.
Wrist images are raw YUYV 640x480 inside the MCAP (~150-390 MB per 8-21 s segment).
Commercial use, including training commercial models, needs prior written authorization from Linkerbot.

cameras.note: color only (yuv422_yuy2) in /camera_d405/color/image_raw; the hand's palm and four fingers are in view

tracking.note: /vut/pose 6DoF at ~120 Hz (125 Hz measured) with tracking_status and map_state per sample; /vut/status at ~5 Hz

tracking.system: UMI-Dex-Pro-L6 joint encoders (6 channels, raw 0-255, validity flags)
tracking.note: names thumb_roll, thumb_pitch, index_pitch, middle_pitch, ring_pitch, pinky_pitch in the checked segment; actuation path not stated

other: VUT tracking and SLAM map status

unconfirmed: embodiment = robot: the touch comes from the L6-type hand's fingertip sensors, not from the person's skin, and the D405 frames show the hand's black palm and fingers. The person carries it; there is no robot arm. Recorded as a robot hand because the sensor and kinematics are the hand's.
hours 0.83 = sum of rosbag2 metadata.yaml durations over all 251 segments (0.831 h), matching the card's per-task totals (0.25 + 0.15 + 0.14 + 0.14 + 0.15 h).

Contact checked (every 3rd or 8th MCAP chunk): water bottle seg_20 index pad 4.4-6.1 s (finger force up to 981 mN), seg_29 thumb 4.4-6.6 s and index 4.9-6.6 s (up to 1,206 mN); cups seg_29 thumb 4.3-14.4 s (981 mN); nail seg_34 nothing; apple seg_29 index 3 counts for < 0.1 s.
Per-finger force vs taxel sum: in seg_20 force (mN) ran ~10x the finger's taxel sum (e.g. 981 mN vs 98).
Rates measured in seg_20: touch and joints 60.0 Hz, images 30.0 Hz, VUT pose 125 Hz, VUT status 5.1 Hz.
VUT positions span ~0.27 m in seg_20; unit taken as m (geometry_msgs/Pose), frame 'vut_tracker' not documented.

The GitHub UMI-Dex repo (Apache-2.0) documents an older recording setup (D455 + ORB-SLAM3, /hand/can_raw or /hand/usart_raw) than this release (VUT, /hand/touch_state); its link to this dataset is the card's 'SDK access' line.
objects = 5 counts object types (cups, nail, water bottle, apple model, green cube); the cup task uses 6 cups.
Linkerbot also publishes CCF-Dexterous-Assembly-Dataset and Linkerhand-Open-World-Dataset on ModelScope; not checked for tactile.

Sensing principle not stated by the release; the catalog's hardware entry linker_hand lists Linker 6x12 fingertip arrays as piezoresistive (L20 / L20 Lite manuals). Whether the UMI-Dex-Pro-L6 uses the same arrays is not stated; the 360-value 12x6-per-finger layout matches.

download.format: <task>/umi_dex_pro_l6_<task>.tar (uncompressed, + checksums.txt) -> '<Task Name>/seg_N/seg_N_0.mcap' (ROS2 MCAP, cdr, uncompressed chunks of ~1.2 MB) + metadata.yaml
download.per_episode: MCAP 147-394 MB per segment (raw YUYV video dominates)
download.partial_fetch: HTTP range reads on the TAR (CDN redirect from the ModelScope repo URL): walk 512-byte TAR headers to get each MCAP's offset, read the MCAP footer + summary (chunk index), then fetch single chunks; touch-only reads still pull the interleaved images (no multi-range support)

channels.name: /hand/touch_state touch_matrix
channels.frame: per finger 12 rows x 6 columns, row-major; finger order 'STM32_FINGER_ORDER'
channels.note: hwk_valid_mask bits 0-4 (thumb..little) = 31 in all checked messages

channels.name: /hand/touch_state finger_force_mn
channels.frame: per finger: thumb, index, middle, ring, little
channels.note: force_valid_mask bit i = fresh reading; 0 with the bit unset is a placeholder. Mask 31 in all checked messages

channels.name: /hand/joint_states
channels.shape: names string[6], positions float64[6], valid bool[6]
channels.frame: thumb roll, thumb pitch, index, middle, ring, pinky pitch
channels.note: aligned with touch_state by firmware seq

channels.name: /vut/pose
channels.shape: Pose (position xyz, quaternion) + vut_timestamp_ms, sequence, tracking_status, map_state
channels.note: end-effector 6D pose per the card; tracking_status 2 = OK throughout seg_20

channels.name: /vut/status
channels.shape: VutStatus (tracking_status, map_state, map_id, sequence, last_pose_age_ms, tracker_sn, failure_hint, paired)

sample.fetch_estimate: ~1.1 GB for the 5 MCAPs (193 + 340 + 204 + 193 + 202 MB) plus ~0.2 GB per replacement segment; already fetched ~180 MB of sampled chunks for the survey. Re-hosted media: YUYV 640x480 re-encoded to H.264, ~5-10 MB per clip. Episode JSON: 360 uint8 + 5 forces at 60 Hz x <= 21 s ~ 0.46M values, under 2 MB if stored compactly.
sample.rules_applied: Tasks: 5 <= 6, so all 5. Episodes: one per task (5 > 3 tasks), 5 in total. Each must be 10-60 s (segments 8.3-21.3 s; 18-50 per task qualify), have touch_state with valid masks, and show contact (taxels or finger force above rest) for >= 1 s. Contact was checked on every 8th MCAP chunk (~0.5 s spacing) for 4 picks; 2 pass, 2 need replacement, 1 unchecked.
